parsed.basis: Nothing formal — just ordinary courtesy and a bit of self-interest. There's no rule in Singapore telling pedestrians which side to pass on; the keep-left idea exists for escalators and some walkways but isn't a law for footpaths. I gave way because she was distracted by her phone and pulling a suitcase, so she was less likely to adjust than I was.
parsed.applies_to: All three decisions — carrying on, then stepping right twice to give her room
parsed.side_detail: The right wall was only 0.41 m away and my body is 0.50 m wide, so I was already close to it — but the space to my right let me clear her path since she was 11 degrees to my left, pulling a suitcase. Moving right put me further from her and nearer the wall I could already feel, and it kept her on the side she was already on rather than pushing her.
